'''Donald Lawson Turcotte''' (April 22, 1932 – February 4, 2025) was an American geophysicist most noted for his work on the boundary layer theory of [[mantle convection]] as part of the theory of [[plate tectonics]].<ref name="Gates">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Turcotte, Donald L. (1932&ndash;)|last1=Gates|first1=Alexander E.|encyclopedia=A to Z of earth scientists|date=2003|publisher=Facts on File|location=New York|isbn=9781438109190|pages=265&ndash;266}}</ref> He worked at Cornell University then the [[University of California, Davis]].

==Life and career==
Turcotte trained as an engineer and earned a PhD in aeronautics and physics from the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) in 1958. After a year at the [[Naval Postgraduate School]] in Monterey, Turcotte took up a position at [[Cornell University]], in the graduate school of Aeronautical Engineering.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://honors.agu.org/winners/donald-l-turcotte/ | title=Donald L. Turcotte }}</ref> In 1965, Turcotte took a sabbatical at the [[University of Oxford]], in the engineering department. Here he met [[Ron Oxburgh]], who had recently arrived in the Department of Geology, and they began a collaboration in which they developed ideas about convective flow in the Earth's mantle, and its links to the newly emerging ideas of [[plate tectonics]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.3035524 | doi=10.1063/1.3035524 | title=Continental drift | year=1969 | last1=Turcotte | first1=Donald L. | last2=Oxburgh | first2=E. Ronald | journal=Physics Today | volume=22 | issue=4 | pages=30–39 | bibcode=1969PhT....22d..30T | url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1973, Turcotte moved to the geology department at Cornell where he worked for the next thirty years. After retiring from Cornell in 2003, Turcotte moved to [[University of California, Davis]].

He has won awards including the [[Arthur L. Day Medal]] of the [[Geological Society of America]], the [[William Bowie Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://honors.agu.org/winners/donald-l-turcotte|title=Bowie Medal Citation|website=www.agu.org|access-date=2016-07-28}}</ref> and the [[Charles A. Whitten Medal]] of the [[American Geophysical Union]]. He was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/donald-l-turcotte-ee8h7v/|title=Donald Turcotte|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2016-07-22}}</ref>

In 2008, the [[American Geophysical Union]]'s Nonlinear Geophysics committee established the Donald L. Turcotte Award, which is given annually to one honoree "in recognition of outstanding dissertation research that contributes directly to nonlinear geophysics."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ng.agu.org/honors/turcotte-award/|title=Donald L. Turcotte Award|website=www.agu.org|access-date=2016-08-06}}</ref>

Turcotte died on February 4, 2025, at the age of 92.<ref>{{cite web |title=Donald L. Turcotte |url=https://www.smith-funerals.com/obituaries/donald-turcotte |website=Smith Funeral Home |access-date=18 February 2025}}</ref>

== Books ==
* Donald L. Turcotte and [[Gerald Schubert]], Geodynamics, [[Cambridge University Press]], Third Edition (2014), {{ISBN|978-1-107-00653-9}} (Hardback) {{ISBN|978-0-521-18623-0}} (Paperback)
* Donald L. Turcotte, Fractals and chaos in geology and geophysics, Cambridge University Press, 1997
* Gerald Schubert, Donald L. Turcotte, and Peter Olson, Mantle convection in the Earth and planets, Cambridge University Press, 2001
